raw:
Reasoning first.

The request — "simulate nitrate transport from fertilized fields to drinking-water wells and estimate arrival concentrations" — is a reactive solute-transport problem in the saturated zone. Decomposed, it needs: (1) a nitrogen source term (fertilizer application + soil N leaching below the root zone), (2) vertical recharge carrying that nitrate downward, (3) lateral saturated groundwater flow along flow paths to well screens, and (4) reactive transport (denitrification, dispersion) yielding a concentration and travel time at each well. Only ONE of these — the vertical water flux (recharge/drainage, QDRAI) that would carry leachate below the root zone — is something the current ELM stack can produce. Everything else is blocked by hard execution limits.

Critically, ELM is single-column with NO lateral transport and NO regional water table, so it cannot move water or solute from a field to a well. ELM's water partitioning does not carry a nitrate species at all, and PFLOTRAN as available is steady-state groundwater FLOW, not the transient reactive N transport this needs. The ELM→PFLOTRAN coupler is not implemented. Therefore the primary deliverable — arrival concentrations at wells — is NOT answerable as posed. Presenting an ELM campaign as if it estimated well nitrate would be dishonest.

What is defensible: use ELM spatial sampling to characterize the recharge/deep-drainage flux across the basin under its land-use/soil mosaic — i.e., the top boundary flux that a future coupled transport model would need. This requires spin-up (or WTD-informed warm start) because recharge is a slow state. The single listed observation (well nitrate) cannot validate an ELM run; there is no in-domain flux or SWE observation given, so validation of the recharge estimate is a gap. I therefore scope this as a partial/infeasible design: deliver the recharge driver field, and list the full transport chain as required capabilities.

I place a small stratified set of columns across the modest 160 m relief and the agricultural mosaic to bracket recharge variability; N is kept small because it only feeds a boundary-flux characterization, not the (impossible) concentration estimate.
